discovery: Photonic crystals and photonic bandgap control of light, including photonic crystal fibres

nominees.name: Philip St. J. Russell
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light, Erlangen, Germany

motivation: In 1987 Yablonovitch and John independently showed that a periodic dielectric structure can open a photonic bandgap. Inside such a structure, spontaneous emission can be suppressed and light can be strongly localized, much as electrons are controlled in semiconductor crystals. Yablonovitch then gave the first experimental demonstration of a full three-dimensional bandgap. John's theory of photon localization and of atom-photon bound states laid the foundations of cavity and waveguide quantum optics in structured media. Russell turned these ideas into photonic crystal fibres, which guide light by microstructure, including in hollow cores. These fibres made supercontinuum sources possible and have advanced frequency metrology, gas-based nonlinear optics and ultrafast science. Together, these discoveries created a new physics of engineered optical media. Photonic crystal concepts now underpin nanophotonic cavities, low-threshold nanolasers, integrated quantum light sources and new optical fibre technologies used worldwide.
